title: Undo the last commit
concept: git reset --soft HEAD~1 keeps your changes

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: I committed too early. The message says "WIP" and it is only half done.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Undo the commit but keep the work. That is `git reset --soft HEAD~1`.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `HEAD~1` means "one commit before where I am now".

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `--soft` is the gentle one. The commit goes away, your file changes stay staged.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: There is also `git reset --hard`. That throws your changes away for real. We will not practise it.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: After the reset, commit again with a proper message.

items.text: The WIP commit is gone and the work is not lost
Commit again with a real message

hints: Undo the commit without losing the work, then commit it properly.
`git reset --soft HEAD~1` removes the last commit and leaves the changes staged.
Run `git reset --soft HEAD~1`, then `git commit -m "Add Riverside Park location"`.
recap: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` undoes the last commit and keeps your changes staged, ready to commit again properly.

cheatSheet.summary: Undo the last commit, keep the changes staged

predict.question: What happens to your text after `git reset --soft HEAD~1`?

choices.text: It is deleted along with the commit
It stays, sitting in the staging area

predict.explanation: `--soft` only moves the branch pointer back. Your files and the staging area are untouched.
